Context dependence of reported model matrices

Source: R/ctContextDependence.R
ctContextDependence.Rd

A ctsem matrix cell may be an expression of a latent process or a time dependent predictor, such as DRIFT[1,1] = '-log1p(exp(param)) * eta2'. Such a cell has a value only at a given evaluation context: a latent state, a set of time dependent predictor values, a time and an interval.

Details

ctsem's summaries and plots report a number for every cell, so for such a model they evaluate it at one of two points, depending on the function:

  • Population matrices (summary, ctSummaryMatrices, ctDiscretePars(subjects='popmean'), ctTIpredEffects) are evaluated at the population T0MEANS state, with time dependent predictors at zero.

  • Subject matrices (ctSubjectPars, ctDiscretePars(subjects=)) are evaluated at each subject's last observed row.

ctKalman and ctPredict evaluate every cell at every step of the filter, so they report no single point.

References to an individually varying parameter are not affected, since the subject's estimate of such a parameter uses all of that subject's data. Only references to dynamic processes and to time dependent predictors make a reported value depend on the evaluation point.

Functions affected by this attach the cells as attr(x, 'contextDependent'), and give a message naming the point. ctModelIsNonlinear reports whether a model has such cells. With backend='julia' the evaluation point can be chosen with the state argument of ctSummaryMatrices, ctDiscretePars, ctExtract and ctNetwork: 'T0MEANS', 'mean' (the mean smoothed latent state), 'asymptotic' (the fixed point the processes settle at), or a numeric vector with one value per latent process. ctPhasePortrait and ctStateDependencePlot show how the dynamics change over the state.

See also

ctModelIsNonlinear, ctSummaryMatrices, ctPhasePortrait, ctStateDependencePlot

Examples

# \donttest{
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
# The auto effect of eta1 changes with the level of eta2, so DRIFT[1, 1]
# has a value only at a given state of eta2.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'),
  PARS = c('a|-log1p_exp(param)', 'b'),
  DRIFT = matrix(c('a + b * eta2', 'drift21', 0, 'drift22'), 2, 2),
  CINT = matrix(c('cint1', 'cint2'), 2, 1), MANIFESTMEANS = 0)
model$pars$indvarying <- FALSE
fit <- ctFit(ctsemtestdat, model)
print(ctModelIsNonlinear(fit))

# The population matrices at the default point, which the message names
# as the T0MEANS state, with time dependent predictors at zero. The
# attribute lists the cells that depend on the point.
m <- ctSummaryMatrices(fit)
print(m$estimate$DRIFT)
print(attr(m, 'contextDependent'))

# DRIFT[1, 1] at the fixed point the processes settle at, at the mean of
# the smoothed latent states, and at a chosen state with eta1 at 8 and
# eta2 at 14.
print(ctSummaryMatrices(fit, state = 'asymptotic')$estimate$DRIFT)
print(ctSummaryMatrices(fit, state = 'mean')$estimate$DRIFT)
print(ctSummaryMatrices(fit, state = c(8, 14))$estimate$DRIFT)
}
# }
